facts.fact: Varun read the crossing party aloud at the post gate the night before: three wardens and two guides. Rohan struck the third warden's name at dawn, so only two wardens went into the gully. Meera heard this, so 'three wardens and two goat-folk' could only have come from the written plan.
facts.why: needed because the beat's clue (C09) requires a specific, checkable number that only the approach plan held.

facts.fact: Lalit is Asha's tracker, a thin young man bound to her by rope and carrying a spyglass. Asha's second pair stays at the camp, unnamed.
facts.why: needed because the beat names Lalit as the boaster and Asha's four make two bound pairs.

facts.fact: Asha gives Meera the whole day and the next until the light goes; after that she comes down with four.
facts.why: needed because the parley needs a deadline for pressure.

facts.fact: Firewood count: thirty-one sticks after the first night, thirty after Rohan's first refusal, twenty-nine after the second.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Rohan burn two sticks and the count is a running device.

facts.fact: Rohan knows the Neshar-side road from walking it as a boy with his father and from mapping the post's end of it. He names a herdsmen's cut above the third bend, behind a stone fold, and a shrine on the way.
facts.why: needed because the beat has him describe the hunters' road before collapsing.

facts.fact: Rohan has a lung fever with a rattling cough that has been building unspoken; it comes to a crisis at the end of chapter 10.
facts.why: needed because the beat ends with his collapse and burning skin.
